name: Dwarf
summary: In Khaz Modan, dwarves keep to the mountain homes they carved from stone. Once earthen, they changed under the Curse of Flesh and now live across Khaz Modan and beyond. King Magni Bronzebeard rules from Ironforge, beneath the peaks of Dun Morogh, a steadfast heart of the Alliance.

sections.title: Sons of the Mountain
sections.body:
Dwarves began as earthen, beings forged by the titans who slept for ages in Uldaman's vaults. The Curse of Flesh changed them into creatures of blood and bone. They took the name dwarves and made their home in Khaz Modan, named for the titan Khaz'goroth. Beneath Dun Morogh's peaks, they carved the stronghold of Ironforge.

Their bodies endure hardship, and their keen eyes find stone and ore. They bring fierce resolve to the forge and to battle. Their halls ring with roaring hearths, and ale is a favored drink.

sections.title: The War of the Three Hammers
sections.body:
After High King Modimus Anvilmar died, the dwarves fought over Ironforge. The Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron clans each sought power, and their struggle became a civil war. The Bronzebeards took the mountain and drove the other clans out.

Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan of the Dark Irons then waged war against both rivals. His forces were driven beneath the Redridge Mountains, where Thaurissan accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. Flames consumed the Dark Iron realm, leaving the volcanic wastes of Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes. The survivors became slaves beneath Blackrock Mountain. The Wildhammers, their home devastated, migrated north to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands.

sections.title: Steadfast Shield of the Alliance
sections.body:
When the Horde swept across the continent in the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard shut Ironforge's gates against its sieges. Dwarven forces fought beside the Alliance of Lordaeron in heavy plate armor and with muskets, while gryphon riders took to the sky. Their courage helped break the Horde.

Ironforge remains one of the Alliance's steadfast defenders. The dwarves have also welcomed their displaced gnome cousins into their halls. Across Khaz Modan, they uncover titan ruins in search of answers about their ancient origins.

faq.q: Where did the dwarves come from originally?
faq.answer: Dwarves descend from the earthen, living stone beings made by the titan keepers. The earthen slept in Uldaman's vaults until the Curse of Flesh changed them into mortal dwarves. Then they settled the mountains of Khaz Modan.

faq.q: Who rules the dwarves right now?
faq.answer: King Magni Bronzebeard rules the Kingdom of Ironforge and the Bronzebeard clan from the Great Forge. He led his people through the Second and Third Wars and remains one of the founding pillars of the Grand Alliance.

faq.q: What are the three main dwarven clans?
faq.answer: The three major clans are the Bronzebeards, who rule Ironforge and Dun Morogh; the Wildhammers, who live in the open air of the Hinterlands and ride gryphons; and the Dark Irons, who live beneath Blackrock Mountain under Ragnaros's fiery dominion.

faq.q: Why are the Dark Iron dwarves enemies?
faq.answer: During the War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Irons tried to destroy both the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans. Facing defeat, their sorcerer-thane summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The flames shattered their homeland, and bound the clan to serve elemental fire and shadow beneath Blackrock Mountain.

faq.q: Why are gnomes living inside Ironforge?
faq.answer: Dwarves and gnomes have shared a close bond for centuries, trading stoneworking secrets for mechanical engineering. When Gnomeregan fell to a trogg invasion and toxic radiation, King Magni gave High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the refugees shelter in Tinker Town.

faq.q: Do dwarves worship the Holy Light?
aliases: do dwarves believe in the light
faq.answer: Yes. Many Ironforge dwarves follow the Holy Light, which humans introduced to them. Dwarven priests keep their own teachings, and stout-hearted dwarves have recently joined the Order of the Silver Hand as paladins.
Dwarves train as warriors, paladins, hunters, rogues, priests and shaman.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you carry a legacy of living stone. Your clans have old blood feuds, and you dig through titan ruins for answers about your origins.
The dwarves are your oldest and truest allies. They helped build Gnomeregan's first stonework and now shelter your people in Tinker Town.
Ironforge's mineral wealth, siege craft and steadfast infantry help guard the Alliance's northern reaches.
As a paladin, you carry the Holy Light with the resolve of Khaz Modan, joining human teachings with dwarven martial discipline.
Dwarven smiths are renowned across Azeroth. The Great Forge's volcanic heat helps them temper arms and armor.
As a dwarf, you have a keen eye for ore and gemstones buried beneath the earth.
